justifications.functional_suitability: Real-Time Scoring Engine covers scoring (R-01) and Case Management Backend & UI covers review (R-02). Model & Rule Synchronizer's atomic swap supports no-downtime updates (R-03). Gaps: no routing of review cases into case management, no decision explanation or model version storage, no model deployment pipeline.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Feature Store (ElastiCache Redis) gives sub-ms lookups, embedded ONNX in Inference & Rule Executor avoids network calls, and Audit Dispatcher with SQS Audit Buffer keeps logging off the hot path. Gaps: no autoscaling stated, extra API Gateway hop, and the Feature Retrieval API adds an unexplained layer.
justifications.compatibility: Merchant / Payment Gateway integration via REST/HTTPS (gRPC at context level) and OAuth2/OIDC with the External IdP are named. Gaps: the IdP is absent from the container relationships, API contracts are undefined, and the REST vs gRPC inconsistency is unresolved.
justifications.usability: Fraud Analyst, Risk Operations Manager and Compliance Auditor are served by the React Analyst Web App with WebSocket queue updates. Gaps: the auditor reaches audit data only through the case UI with no explicit Athena path, and no dashboards, explanation views or merchant developer interface are shown.
justifications.reliability: SQS Audit Buffer decouples logging and managed Fargate/ElastiCache are used. But R-07 has no fail-open fallback, there is no multi-AZ, replication, circuit breaker or retry design, and Redis is a single point of failure for scoring. Nothing guarantees audit write durability before decisions.
justifications.security: AWS WAF, TLS, IdP MFA, RBAC and data masking in FastAPI Case Management Backend, and S3 Object Lock WORM address integrity and audit. Gaps: no tokenization or encryption/KMS mechanism, no PCI network segmentation, no service-to-service authentication, and no storage of explanation or model version.
justifications.maintainability: Decomposition is clear, with separate containers and components like Model & Rule Synchronizer, Audit Dispatcher and Feature Assembler. Gaps: inconsistent duplicate elements (Audit Log Storage repeated, API Gateway as a component of the engine), mixed Go/Python/Node stacks for a three-person team, and extra RDS.
justifications.portability: The design is tightly bound to AWS services (Lambda, SQS, S3 Object Lock, Athena, ElastiCache, Fargate), with only eu-west-1 required. Containers (ECS Fargate, ONNX open model format) help somewhat, but there is no abstraction or IaC to replace infrastructure.

sensitivity_points: API Gateway hop adds latency to the 50 ms budget
Redis lookup latency under load
Feature Retrieval API Go layer adds a hop
tradeoffs: Managed gateway convenience versus latency overhead
Embedded ONNX speed versus model flexibility
PERF-01.justification: In-process ONNX, Redis features and async audit suit the target. But no autoscaling or sizing, no capacity evidence, and API Gateway plus an extra Feature Retrieval API hop risk P99 under 50 ms.

sensitivity_points: Case data store is not defined
Shared Redis or S3 access could contend with scoring
tradeoffs: Separate containers isolate load versus higher cost
Static SPA via CloudFront speeds screens but adds complexity
PERF-02.justification: The case UI is a separate Fargate service with a CDN-hosted SPA, so it is isolated from scoring. But there is no case database, queue store or read model, and the case-to-scoring data path is unclear. Risks are unaddressed.

sensitivity_points: No fallback decision path defined
No redundancy or health checks specified
tradeoffs: Fallback approving risks fraud; fallback declining risks blocking payments
AVAIL-01.justification: No fallback path, circuit breaker, multi-AZ deployment or default-decision mechanism exists. Fallback decisions are not audited. A crash of scoring would block payments, so the requirement is not met.

sensitivity_points: Audit Dispatcher flush is async but has no local buffer
Container-level link writes to S3 directly, bypassing SQS
Dispatcher-to-SQS link is missing
tradeoffs: Async buffering protects latency but risks loss on a crash
Serverless ingestion saves cost but adds delay
AVAIL-02.justification: An SQS buffer and Lambda decouple audit writes from scoring. But the dispatcher's wiring is inconsistent: it writes straight to S3, no durable local buffering or DLQ is stated, and no-loss is not guaranteed.

sensitivity_points: Atomic swap is in-process per instance
No rollback or version registry
Model version not recorded in audit
tradeoffs: Hot swap avoids downtime but lacks staged rollout or canary
MOD-01.justification: The atomic.Value swap gives zero-downtime activation, and models are stored in S3. But there is no rollback procedure, no versioning or canary, no notification trigger, and no explicit recording of the model version in decisions.

sensitivity_points: No rule authoring or approval component
Rule explanation not captured
Rule-set versioning absent
tradeoffs: Embedded rules are fast but harder for analysts to edit
MOD-02.justification: Rules are embedded and can be hot-swapped, but no rule authoring interface, approval workflow, or rule distribution is modeled. Nothing records applied rules or an explanation per decision. Analyst-driven change within an hour is unsupported.

sensitivity_points: Data masking is only mentioned in a description
No anomaly detection or alerting component
No tokenization service shown
tradeoffs: Masking in the backend is simple but is a single point of failure
SEC-01.justification: RBAC, MFA via the IdP and masking exist in the backend, and access is audited. But no tokenization or vault, no anomaly detection or alerting within 15 minutes, and no guarantee that card data stays out of analyst-reachable stores.

sensitivity_points: Audit payload content not specified to include explanation
Model artifacts retention for 7 years not specified
Object Lock compliance mode and Athena aid retrieval
tradeoffs: WORM storage ensures integrity but prevents correction and deletion
SEC-02.justification: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode, partitioned logs, Athena queries and feature snapshots support retrieval of tamper-evident records. But explanations, model version and rules aren't shown as stored, and there is no model artifact archive for reproduction.
